title: JC H2 differentiation: connected rates of change
subject: math

complete.problem: The radius of a circle increases at 0.5 cm/s. Find the rate of increase of the area when the radius is 4 cm.

steps.text: Write the link equation: A = pi r^2, so dA/dr = 2 pi r.
steps.annotation: The area depends on the radius, so differentiate A with respect to r.

steps.text: Apply the chain rule: dA/dt = (dA/dr)(dr/dt) = 2 pi r x 0.5.
steps.annotation: The chain rule connects the rate we want to the rate we are given.

steps.text: Substitute r = 4: dA/dt = 2 pi (4)(0.5) = 4 pi, about 12.6 cm^2/s.
steps.annotation: Substitute only at the end, once the rate expression is in terms of r.

complete.selfExplanation: Explain why the chain rule is needed here instead of differentiating A with respect to t directly.

faded.problem: The side of a square increases at 2 cm/s. Find the rate of increase of the area when the side is 10 cm.

steps.text: Write the link equation: A = x^2, so dA/dx = 2x.
steps.annotation: The area depends on the side x, so differentiate with respect to x.

steps.text: Apply the chain rule: dA/dt = (dA/dx)(dx/dt) = 2x x 2 = 4x.
steps.annotation: Multiply the derivative by the given rate dx/dt = 2 cm/s.
The area grows faster as the square gets bigger, because dA/dt depends on x.

faded.selfExplanation: The first step is shown. Write down the chain-rule statement you would use next.

paired.problem: The radius of a sphere decreases at 0.1 cm/s. Find the rate of decrease of the volume when the radius is 5 cm. (V = 4/3 pi r^3.)
paired.solution: dV/dr = 4 pi r^2. By the chain rule, dV/dt = (dV/dr)(dr/dt) = 4 pi r^2 x (-0.1). At r = 5: dV/dt = 4 pi (25)(-0.1) = -10 pi, about -31.4 cm^3/s, so the volume decreases at about 31.4 cm^3/s.
